The definite and indefinite integrals of a fractal function are explicitly evaluated, using the fractal property which states that any . x ∈ I is described as an image of compositions of functions. Further, the integral of non-affine fractal interpolation functions namely, the . α -fractal function, hidden variable fractal function and A-fractal function are investigated with constant and variable scaling factors. This study clearly acknowledges that the integral of different types of fractal functions generate new fractal functions whenever they satisfy the endpoint conditions.

In the evolution of fractal interpolation theory, many researchers have constructed various types of non-affine fractal functions to amplify the flexibility in approximation, the . α -fractal function is one among the classic example of non-affine fractal functions. In general, the fractal properties such as fractal dimension, smoothness of fractal function are much influenced by the free parameter called the vertical scaling factor. Most of the research works on the FIF have been studied with constant scaling factors which obviously provide self-similar character. Since there exists nonuniform data (or functions) showing less self-similarity, for this type of functions, variable scaling factors could be the better choice instead of constant scaling factors. This chapter discusses the fractional integral of non-affine fractal functions with variable scaling parameters. Additionally, a fractional operator developed in relation with . α -fractal function is presented and some analytical properties such as linearity, boundedness of the fractional operator are discussed with respect to the order of Riemann-Liouville fractional integral.

context_after.text: With these advantages of Weyl-Marchaud fractional derivative, this chapter covers the study of Weyl-Marchaud fractional derivative for types of fractal interpolation functions, where the scaling factors are chosen as constants. It highlights the choice of fractional order while applying the fractional derivative to fractal functions. Pertinent examples and counter examples are discussed for the particular fractional order choice. In a broader sense, this chapter answers the question, is the fractional derivative of fractal function is again an attractor for a new iterated function system? Further, the relation between the fractional order of Weyl-Marchaud derivative and the scaling factors associated with the fractal functions is explicitly presented.

The first intriguing element for integrating fractal functions and fractional order is the fractal dimension. Fractal sets, fractal functions, and fractal surfaces have noninteger (fractional) fractal dimension, in general. This characteristic has opened up the potential of bridging the two distinct domains of fractal geometry and fractional calculus, see [ 1- 4]. Later, motivated by the merits of fractional calculus, the trend of applying fractional derivative and fractional integral to fractal interpolation functions has gained popularity. One more non-avoidable reason behind this study is the non-differentiable nature of fractal interpolation functions despite they are continuous everywhere. For detailed study on the fractional derivative and fractional integral of fractal functions, interested readers may refer the literature [ 5- 10]. Among the various fractional derivative methods, this chapter concentrates on the Weyl-Marchaud fractional derivative. This particular choice is purely based on its definition, it requires just a continuous function for differentiating with fractional order. λ ∈ ( 0 , 1 ) . This chapter has introduced new fractal functions by differentiating types of fractal interpolation functions with Weyl-Marchaud fractional derivative. It highlights the choice of fractional order depending on the provided fractal scaling factors. Numerical examples are presented to observe how the fractional derivative of fractal functions evolve on increasing the fractional order. For all the different types of fractal functions, their fractional derivative shows more complexity maintaining self-similar property. In general, fractal interpolation functions are developed to approximate naturally existing complex functions. The higher irregularity of fractional derivative of fractal functions ensure that they can be effectively used to approximate highly irregular physical phenomena such as stock price, fluctuations in gold price and ECG signals.

The bidirectional recurrent neural networks have been introduced as unique recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to process the data sequence in both directions [ 51]. They carry over all of the attributes of RNNs and expand their functionality to situations where information from the past and future influences the result. Thus, an LSTM layer and a bidirectional neural layer are combined to form a BiLSTM network. In other words, the Bidirectional layer receives the LSTM application, creating two hidden layers-one for the Forward LSTM and one for the Backward LSTM [ 22]. Due to the two-way inputs in this neural network, the interaction between the inputs is improved, resulting in boosting the quantity of information available in the network.
